title: A dose-finding challenge study of Staphylococcus aureus skin infection in healthy adults
official: SaFESkIn – Staphylococcus aureus Forearm Experimental Skin Infection
summary:
Background and study aims
Staphylococcus aureus (“Staph”) is a very common bacteria that lives harmlessly in the nose and skin of about 3 in 10 healthy adults. In some people, however, it can cause infections – especially after surgery or in those who are more vulnerable. There is currently no vaccine against Staph, and it is getting more difficult to find antibiotics that work well.
This study aims to understand why Staph causes infection in some people’s skin but not others, and how the body responds when this happens. A small amount of bacteria will be dropped onto a participant's forearm, which is then covered by a dressing, this would then stay in place for up to 7 days to watch and see if signs of early skin infection developed.

Who can participate?
Healthy adults aged 18 to 55 years who meet the detailed health and lifestyle criteria set by the study team.

What does the study involve?
Participants will first attend a screening visit, where their general health will be checked. If eligible, they will return to receive the challenge, which means a small amount of Staphylococcus aureus will be dripped onto the forearm. 

Participants will record any symptoms each day for 28 days, with some days involving in-person visits for safety checks, blood tests, swabs from nose, throat and skin. The study team may also collect skin microbiopsies. People with signs of skin infection will be treated with antibiotics.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Participants will be contributing to important research that may help scientists develop new ways to prevent or treat Staphylococcus aureus infections in the future. However, taking part carries some risks. Mild infections of the skin with some pain, tenderness, redness, warmth, and swelling may occur, though more serious infections are uncommon in healthy adults. There is a small chance volunteers could pass the bacteria to others, so they must avoid close contact with vulnerable people for a period of time. Blood tests may cause slight pain or bruising, and nasal swabs and skin microbiopsies can be a little uncomfortable. Antibiotics will only be used if necessary.

Where is the study run from?
The Centre for Clinical Vaccinology and Tropical Medicine at Churchill Hospital, Oxford, UK.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
November 2026 to December 2029.

Who is funding the study?
Ellison Institute of Technology (UK).

Who is the main contact?
Dr Jan Pieter Koopman, the Centre for Clinical Vaccinology and Tropical Medicine in Oxford, jan.koopman@paediatrics.ox.ac.uk

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participants must satisfy all the following criteria to be eligible for the study: 

1.	Adults between 18 to 55 years old (inclusive) at the time of enrolment (defined by the date of challenge)
2.	Medically healthy, such that according to investigator judgement, hospitalisation within the study period is not anticipated, and the participant appears likely to be able to remain a study participant through to the end of protocol-specified follow-up. Planned elective procedures for pre-existing conditions may be allowable if S. aureus colonisation is not deemed to put the participant at increased risk of harm and if the elective procedure does not routinely involve, and is not likely to involve, decolonisation and/or antibiotic therapy.
3.	Fluent spoken English – to ensure a comprehensive understanding of the research project and their proposed involvement
4.	Capacity to provide written informed consent in English for participation in the study
5.	Able to attend the scheduled visits and to comply with all study procedures, including internet access for the recording of electronic diaries
6.	Able to follow and adhere to hygiene advice, dressing care instructions and the decolonisation protocol (if given)
7.	Willing and able to avoid planned, non-essential non-study antibiotics from enrolment until the Day 28 visit
8.	Willing and able to avoid intranasal and inhaled products (including nasal steroids) unless prescribed by the study team from enrolment until the Day 28 visit
9.	Willing to allow confirmation of past medical history either through provision of, or access to, a medical record summary or other medical documentation or to allow investigators to obtain a copy of their medical history via their GP practice or via electronic patient records
10.	Willing to allow their GP and/or consultant, if appropriate, to be notified of participation in the study
11.	Willing to provide their national insurance number or passport number to be registered on The Trial Over-Volunteering Prevention System (TOPS)
12.	For participants of childbearing potential only: Willing to use effective contraception for the duration of the study AND to have a pregnancy test on the day of screening, and challenge or as indicated by the study doctor
Exclusion criteria:
1. Research Participants: 
1.1. Participation in another research study, in which procedures performed could compromise the integrity of this study or the safety of the participant, or are planning to do so within the study period   
2. Vaccination:   
2.1. Planned vaccination in the one month following challenge or 2 weeks preceding challenge 
2.2. Live vaccination within the 4 weeks prior to challenge 
3. Allergy: 
3.1. Have an allergy or intolerance to beta-lactam antibiotics   
3.2. Have an allergy or intolerance to more than one of doxycycline, clarithromycin, cephalexin, co-trimoxazole, clindamycin and linezolid 
3.3. Have an allergy or intolerance to any of the agents used for decolonisation 
3.4. Have an allergy or intolerance towards the wound dressings
3.5. Have an allergy or intolerance to surgical skin markers
4. Specific Health history:
4.1. History of severe S. aureus infection, including PVL-associated disease 
4.2. History of MRSA colonisation or infection 
4.3. Atopic dermatitis 
4.4. Psoriasis, eczema or other chronic skin condition requiring treatment in the last year 
4.5. Autoimmune skin conditions at the discretion of the clinical investigator, including but not limited to alopecia and vitiligo 
4.6. Compromised skin barrier function at the discretion of the investigator 
4.7. Known structural heart issues at the discretion of the investigator, including, but not limited to PFO, VSD, bicuspid AV 
4.8. Implanted prosthetic material including but not limited to cochlear implants, orthopaedic implants, implantable cardiac devices, cardiac valves, neurological stimulators, or dental implants 
4.9. Planned surgical, dental, orthodontic, dental hygienist or pre-operative appointment over the study period 
4.10. Anatomically unable to receive intended method of challenge
4.11. Use of treatments or devices that could compromise the skin barrier function from a week prior to enrolment until the Day 28 visit
4.12. Skin alterations on challenge sites (e.g. tattoos) that would interfere with investigators ability to assess skin infection
5. General Health History: Moderate-severe ill health including but not limited to: 
5.1. Asplenia or dysfunction of the spleen 
5.2. Chronic respiratory disease (e.g., asthma [on medication], COPD, emphysema, bronchiectasis) 
5.3. Chronic heart disease (e.g., angina, ischaemic heart disease, chronic heart failure). 
5.4. Chronic kidney disease (e.g., nephrotic syndrome, kidney transplant, on dialysis) 
5.5. Chronic liver disease (e.g., cirrhosis, biliary atresia, hepatitis) 
5.6. Chronic neurological conditions 
5.7. Connective tissue disease 
5.8. Dementia 
5.9. Diabetes mellitus (including diet controlled) 
5.10. Immunosuppression or history of receiving immunosuppressive therapy – at the discretion of the investigator 
5.11. History of a bleeding disorder (e.g., Factor deficiency, coagulopathy, or platelet disorder, or prior history of significant bleeding or bruising following IM injections or venepuncture 
5.12. Have any uncontrolled medical/surgical/mental health conditions at the discretion of the study doctor 
5.13. Significant mental health condition that would impair the participant’s ability to participate in the study 
5.14. Weight less than 50kg, at investigators discretion
5.15. Obesity, at investigators discretion
6. Taking Medications: 
6.1. Any medication that may affect the immune system in the last 3 months (e.g., systemic steroids [PO/IM/IV], Roaccutane, disease modifying anti-rheumatoid drugs) 
6.2. Concurrent use of topical steroids
6.3. Current or intended long-term/intermittent use of antibiotics over the course of the study 
6.4. Recent systemic antibiotic exposure in the last 1 month 
6.5. Use of any medication affecting blood clotting (any oral/injectable anticoagulants) except for aspirin for secondary cardiovascular prevention 
6.6. Use or intranasal medications within the last 4 weeks 
7. Volunteers:
7.1. Who have close contact in high-risk occupational settings or with high-risk or vulnerable individuals during the study. 
7.2. Who work in commercial food handling
7.3. Who are pregnant, lactating or intending on becoming pregnant during the study   
8. Volunteers who have close contact with individuals at higher risk of infection: 
8.1. Children under 5 years of age 
8.2. Chronic ill health or immunosuppressed adults 
8.3. Older adults ≥65 years of age 
8.4. Close household contact with compromised skin barrier function, psoriasis, eczema or other chronic skin condition requiring treatment in the last year 
9. Smoker: Current or ex-smoker in the last 6 months 
10. Suspected or known current hazardous or harmful alcohol or drug use, as per investigators’ discretion   
11. Intended overseas travel from enrolment until Day 14
12. Unable to take digital photos
13. Any other issue which, in the opinion of the study staff, may: 
13.1. Put the participant or their contacts at risk because of participation in the study 
13.2. Adversely affect the interpretation of the study results, or 
13.3. Impair the participant’s ability to participate in the study
14. Study staff or a partner or dependent child of study staff
